brief: Verdict ahead of the print: the reported numbers will be small and probably still loss-making at the EBITDA line; the stock will trade on Lake Mariner delivery dates and on how Justified gets financed.

Where expectations sit. Yahoo Finance shows a Q3 revenue consensus of $64.3M from 14 analysts (range $56.2M to $79.5M), against $44.8M in Q2 and $50.6M a year ago. EPS consensus is -$0.38, but only 2 analysts contribute. We could not find a published Q3 adjusted EBITDA consensus. Needham's full-year 2026 numbers ($230M revenue, $26M adjusted EBITDA, cut in August from $393M and $200M) imply the second half has to deliver roughly $151M of revenue against $78.8M in the first half, so most of the year's EBITDA must land in Q3 and Q4.

What the quarter should show. CB-3 was delivered in early July, lifting revenue-generating HPC capacity from 81 MW to 102 MW, so Q3 gets a full quarter of that step-up. CB-4's first hall was targeting its contractual milestone in late September, with the rest of CB-4 phased through Q4 and CB-5 starting in early January 2027. Those dates are already about one quarter later than planned because Fluidstack changed the design; TeraWulf says the new dates were mutually agreed, with no delay penalties. Bitcoin mining, $12.8M of Q2 revenue, is shrinking and bitcoin was trading near $80,000 to $82,000 in mid-October.

Three debates. First, delivery: did CB-4 hit its late-September milestone, and how many MW are paying rent at 30 September and at year-end? Another slip would push the 2026 numbers below even Needham's reduced estimates. Second, Justified financing: the 20-year Anthropic lease (about 401 MW, about $19B of initial contracted revenue) still lacked finalized investment-grade credit support as of KBW's July note, and Bloomberg reported a roughly $3.5B leveraged loan and high-yield package led by Morgan Stanley. That has to price into a market where CoreWeave's 2032 bonds traded as high as 15% yield and the 10-year Treasury sat around 5.0% to 5.4% in mid-October. Third, the balance sheet: at 30 June TeraWulf held about $3.0B of cash and restricted cash against about $3.11B of senior notes and $2.10B of convertibles, $1.10B of them classified as current. Q2 interest expense was $56.4M, more than the $44.8M of total revenue.

What would move the stock. Positive: a named credit-support provider for Justified, a priced debt deal with no parent guarantee, CB-4 rent commencing on time, and a new lease at Muskie, where contracted power doubled to 1 GW on 5 October. Negative: another Fluidstack slip, credit support that is only partial, or a financing plan that leans on equity with the stock near $12 (20 October close), well under half the $33.33 consensus target.

Kona read-through. TeraWulf's economics show what a long, hyperscaler-adjacent lease is worth (KBW's 18.3% trended yield on cost at $10M to $12M per net MW), and also that the lease alone does not unlock cheap debt without investment-grade credit support. Kona should treat the credit wrapper, not the lease rate, as the binding constraint.
checks: No subagent was available, so I reopened every source myself and confirmed each number kept. Q2 release (EDGAR): revenue $44.8M, HPC $31.9M, adjusted EBITDA -$18.3M, net loss $940.8M, warrant loss $755.7M, about $3.0B cash and restricted cash, 81 MW to 102 MW, 336 MW under construction, CB-4 2H26 and CB-5 early 2027 (phased delivery start), Anthropic about 401 MW / 20 years / about $19B / up to about $33B, Justified timing, Google $600M, Abernathy about $530M (agreement, not closed), $8M to $10M per MW, 250 MW to 500 MW target, interest expense $56.4M. 10-Q: convertibles $1,102.0M current and $1,001.1M noncurrent, senior notes $90.7M and $3,019.3M, warrants $1,816.7M, depreciation $21.2M, H1 purchases of plant and equipment $1,378.5M, capex not yet paid $530.6M, all Core42 leases commenced. Needham article: estimate cuts, Q2 estimates, CB-4 and CB-5 timing, one-quarter slip, no penalties, $150M fit-out. KBW article: 18.3%, $10M to $12M per net MW (management guidance including smelter retirement), 85% NOI margin, 401/482 MW, no investment-grade support, Abernathy installments. Yahoo: $64.31M consensus, 14 analysts, range, year-ago $50.58M, no EBITDA estimate. MarketBeat: $14.685 on 5 October, $33.33 target. CoinDesk: Prager's comment of about $9M per MW, CoreWeave 2032 bonds as high as 15%, 10-year about 5.04% to 5.36%. Muskie 8-K: 1 GW, 2028 and 2029 phases. The roughly $3.5B financing appears only in Bloomberg as relayed by Stocktwits and is not in any filing (unverified). The $197 per kW-month figure is our own calculation. No Q3 adjusted EBITDA consensus was found. CB-4's September milestone has not been confirmed by any company announcement found.
headline: Q3 is a delivery-and-funding test, not a revenue test: the market will judge whether CB-4 rent started on the slipped schedule and whether the Anthropic campus at Justified has signed credit support and debt at a price that still works.
kona: TeraWulf shows that a 20-year hyperscaler-tier lease earns a high-teens yield on cost, and that even so, the debt waits on investment-grade credit support. Kona, at tens of MW without a hyperscaler wrapper, should expect lenders to price the tenant, not the asset. That argues for prepayments, parent guarantees or letters of credit from any GPU-owner tenant before Kona commits capex. Lake Mariner's slip also argues for contract terms that make the tenant pay for design changes (as Fluidstack now does, at cost plus a margin) and that do not reset delivery penalties.

name: TeraWulf

questions.question: In August you told us CB-4's first hall would hit its contractual milestone in late September, after Fluidstack's design changes had already cost a quarter, and 2026 consensus EBITDA has fallen from about $200M to the mid-twenties. How many critical IT MW were paying rent on 30 September, and how many will be on 31 December? If any CB-4 hall is now expected to commence after 31 December, which halls, and how much annualized rent does that move into 2027?
questions.why: Q3 and Q4 have to carry almost all of 2026 EBITDA. A second slip would hurt credibility, because these dates are what support the 2027 and 2028 valuation.

questions.question: KBW put the Anthropic lease at an 18.3% trended yield on cost, but in July there was still no finalized investment-grade credit support, and since then CoreWeave paper has traded at 15%. Is the Justified backstop signed, who provides it, and what share of the 20-year rent does it cover? What all-in coupon do you expect on the roughly $3.5B financing, and is it non-recourse to the parent? If the support is partial, will you fill the gap with a parent guarantee or with equity?
questions.why: The project's equity return depends on the spread between yield on cost and cost of debt. A partial wrapper or a parent guarantee would change the credit quality of the whole company.

questions.question: At 30 June you had about $3.0B of cash and restricted cash, $1.10B of convertibles classified as current, $530.6M of capex incurred but not yet paid, and quarterly interest of $56.4M against $44.8M of revenue. Through which date are CB-4, CB-5 and Justified's equity share fully funded? Will you settle the current convertibles in cash or in shares? What is the maximum share issuance you would accept before Justified's debt closes?
questions.why: With the stock near $12, settling in shares and issuing equity is the main threat to per-share value.

risks: Another Fluidstack-driven delay at CB-4 or CB-5.
Justified credit support ends up partial or delayed, which raises the coupon or requires a parent guarantee.
Convertible settlement or new equity issued with the stock near $12.
Bitcoin weakness speeds up the decline in mining revenue.
Warrant fair-value swings distort GAAP EPS.

sections.body: TeraWulf owns power-rich former industrial sites and leases finished data halls to AI tenants on 10-year to 20-year terms. The tenants supply their own GPUs. Revenue is fixed rent recognized straight-line, with power passed through at cost. Scale matters because each new site is financed largely against the tenant's credit or a third-party backstop, so contracted MW turn into debt capacity. Bitcoin mining is a shrinking legacy business.
sections.title: Business model

sections.body: Q3 revenue consensus is $64.3M (Yahoo Finance, 14 analysts) and EPS is -$0.38 (2 analysts); we could not find an adjusted EBITDA consensus. Needham cut 2026 to $230M revenue and $26M adjusted EBITDA in August, after Q2 missed its $50M revenue and $8.2M EBITDA estimates. The sell side is valuing 2027 and 2028 (Needham: 20x discounted 2028 EBITDA of $1.32B), so Q3 matters mainly as a check on whether the delivery schedule holds.
sections.title: What the market expects

sections.body: Lake Mariner (Fluidstack, Core42): 102 MW revenue-generating; CB-4 first hall due late September and the rest through Q4; CB-5 from early January 2027; build cost tracking about $9M per critical IT MW against $8M to $10M guidance (CEO, 15 October). Google's $600M credit support for Fluidstack became effective when CB-3 was delivered. Justified (Anthropic): about 401 MW net and 482 MW gross; initial delivery 2H 2027 and full delivery early 2028; Kentucky PSC approved the power agreement in August. By our calculation, $19B over 20 years averages about $197 per kW-month across the term; this is not a disclosed figure. Muskie: contracted power raised to 1 GW on 5 October, with the first 500 MW ramping in 2028 and the second 500 MW in 2029, subject to approval; no tenant yet. Abernathy: sale of the 50.1% stake to a Fluidstack-led group for about $530M, paid as $250M, $150M by 31 December 2026 and about $130M by 30 April 2027. Morgantown (Chesapeake): FERC authorized the acquisition on 29 July, with closing expected in 2H 2026.
sections.title: Drivers to watch

sections.body: At 30 June: about $3.0B of cash and restricted cash; senior notes of $3.11B; convertibles of $2.10B, of which $1.10B is current; warrant liabilities of $1.82B. Q2 interest expense was $56.4M against revenue of $44.8M, and depreciation was $21.2M. TeraWulf funded about $150M of Fluidstack fit-out through 30 June; Fluidstack pays for costs incurred after 5 July in cash plus a margin. According to Bloomberg via Stocktwits, the CFO plans a roughly $3.5B package for Justified (its first leveraged loan plus high-yield bonds, led by Morgan Stanley), but no deal has been announced. KBW said the main overhang is the lack of finalized investment-grade credit support, which depends on which chips Anthropic chooses.
sections.title: Funding and balance sheet

sections.body: Credit markets for AI infrastructure have tightened: CoreWeave's 2032 bonds traded as high as 15% yield and the 10-year Treasury moved above 5%. The tenant has caused one schedule slip at Lake Mariner already. Interest expense exceeds revenue until CB-4 and CB-5 pay rent. The current convertibles may be settled in shares, which would dilute holders. Warrant marks make GAAP results volatile.
sections.title: Emerging risks

sections.body: MW paying rent at 30 September and 31 December; revised CB-4 and CB-5 dates; name, size and scope of the Justified credit support; coupon and recourse of the Justified debt; Abernathy cash received; Morgantown closing; first tenant at Muskie; progress against the 250 MW to 500 MW annual contracting target; interest expense against HPC revenue.
